candidates.title: Tumor expression of dopamine receptor and prolactin is associated with acute dopamine agonist response in acromegaly.
candidates.abstract: In acromegaly, primary treatment is usually pituitary surgery. Remission rates are approximately 50% with pituitary tumor size and invasiveness playing important roles. Medical therapy is the secondary treatment for many patients. Yet, dopamine agonist responsiveness is variable, and reliable prognostic markers are lacking. We aimed to identify markers of dopamine agonist responsiveness. We hypothesized that (i) dopamine agonist response correlates with high dopamine receptor D2 expression and prolactin expression and secretion and (ii) estrogen receptor α expression is associated with tumor properties. Single-center retrospective cohort analysis with treatment-naive patients who had undergone a bromocriptine test as a marker for dopamine agonist response. Sixty-nine patients with newly diagnosed acromegaly between 2008 and 2017 were included. During this period, the bromocriptine test was performed routinely at our center. Baseline hormone concentrations and MR images were evaluated retrospectively. Immunohistochemical staining of hormones and receptors and gene expression of dopamine receptor D2 in tumor tissue were performed and assessed. Dopamine agonist test response and high dopamine receptor D2 gene expression were correlated (r = 0.53; p ≤ 0.001), and both were associated with higher serum prolactin concentration and tumor prolactin expression, assessed by immunohistochemistry. Prolactin and estrogen receptor α expression were correlated, and strong expression was associated with smaller and less invasive tumors. Dopamine receptor D2 and prolactin expression are markers for dopamine agonist test response, providing valuable insights for personalized management and optimization of medical therapy in patients with acromegaly. Although prolactin and estrogen receptor α expression may be associated with tumor growth, the clinical applicability remains unclear.

candidates.title: Gracilis tendon harvest for ACL reconstruction impairs gracilis muscle volume recovery and may adversely affect adjacent thigh musculature. MRI-based outcomes from a subgroup of patients enroled in the DOSTAR randomized controlled trial.
candidates.abstract: Segmentation of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) allows accurate calculation of muscle volumes. The Dual Or Single Tendon Anterior cruciate ligament Reconstruction (DOSTAR) study is a prospective randomized controlled trial investigating a semitendinosus (ST) graft with adjustable button tibial fixation versus a dual tendon semitendinosus and gracilis (STG) graft with screw tibial fixation in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR). The purpose of the present study is to investigate differences in thigh muscle volume at 6 and 12 months between these treatment groups. Patients were randomized and underwent ACLR using either a ST or STG graft construct. MRI of bilateral thighs was completed at 6 and 12 months post-operatively. Muscle volumes were measured in both thighs at both time points in both groups. A total of 38 patients underwent MRI scanning at 6 and 12 months. There was a significant difference in the interval volume change of gracilis in the STG group compared to the ST group (-1.6 cm3 ± 4.6 vs. +2.8 cm3 ± 6.8, p = 0.026). Interval gracilis hypertrophy occurred in 35% (7/20) of cases in the STG group and 67% of cases (12/18) in the ST group (p = 0.103). Adductor longus (AddL) also demonstrated a significant difference in interval volume change between the STG and ST group (-2.4 cm3 ± 12.0 vs. +11.1 cm3 ± 21.2, p = 0.020). AddL hypertrophy occurred in 30% of cases (6/20) in the STG group and 72% (13/18) in the ST group (p = 0.022). All other muscles had no significant differences noted in muscle recovery between groups. Linear regression analysis demonstrated a significant positive relationship between interval changes in gracilis and AddL volumes (p < 0.001). The present study provides MRI evidence that gracilis tendon harvest was associated with persistent impairment of gracilis muscle recovery and may also adversely affect AddL. This adds to the growing body of evidence supporting the use of ST with adjustable button graft constructs for hamstring ACLR. Level II, subgroup analysis of prospective, double-blinded, randomized controlled trial.
candidates.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA

candidates.title: Newly Diagnosed Graves' Disease Followed by the Discovery of a Cavernous Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm Causing Panhypopituitarism: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sellar and parasellar vascular lesions are rare causes of pituitary dysfunction and may mimic pituitary adenomas or other sellar masses. Cavernous internal carotid artery (ICA) aneurysms can cause hypopituitarism through compression of the pituitary gland or stalk, but diagnosis may be delayed when symptoms are initially attributed to a more common endocrine disorder. We report a 37-year-old man who presented with six weeks of unintentional weight loss, fatigue, heat intolerance, excessive sweating, anxiety, tremor, and tachycardia. Initial evaluation showed suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), elevated total triiodothyronine (T3), positive thyrotropin receptor antibody, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin, and a hypervascular thyroid gland on ultrasound, consistent with Graves' disease. He was started on methimazole and atenolol. Although thyroid function tests improved, he developed persistent neck discomfort, prompting contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), which revealed an enhancing sellar mass. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a T2-hypointense sellar lesion with internal flow artifact, and CT angiography confirmed a saccular aneurysm of the cavernous segment of the right ICA. Pituitary hormone evaluation demonstrated secondary adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, growth hormone (GH) deficiency, and mild hyperprolactinemia, consistent with panhypopituitarism from pituitary compression. The patient was started on prednisone and levothyroxine, and atenolol and prednisone were subsequently discontinued before endovascular embolization was performed. At follow-up, symptoms improved, but panhypopituitarism persisted. This case highlights the importance of reassessing patients when endocrine symptoms evolve despite an initially appropriate diagnosis.

candidates.title: Transfemoral transcaval adrenal biopsy: a technical report and review of adrenal biopsy approaches.
candidates.abstract: Despite advances in cross-sectional imaging, adrenal biopsy plays a role in a small subset of lesions that remain indeterminate after complete imaging work-up or in which tissue diagnosis would alter management. Anatomic constraints around the adrenal glands can make safe percutaneous access technically challenging. This technical report describes a transfemoral transcaval approach to biopsy of a right adrenal mass directly abutting the inferior vena cava (IVC) that was not safely accessible by conventional percutaneous routes. Additionally, a concise review of contemporary adrenal biopsy indications and access routes is performed. Adapted from transfemoral transcaval liver biopsy, the technique uses right common femoral venous access, positioning of a reshaped metal guide cannula within the IVC at the level of the lesion adjacent to the right renal vein, and deployment of a core biopsy needle across the caval wall under combined fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance, with cone-beam CT confirmation of needle position and completion venography to exclude caval injury. Diagnostic tissue was obtained without periprocedural complication; histopathology demonstrated an unexpected pheochromocytoma, a finding discussed here in detail due to its implications for pre-procedure biochemical evaluation. This limited experience demonstrates technical feasibility in carefully selected patients. The safety and comparative effectiveness of the technique require evaluation in larger series.

candidates.title: Improving the subtyping of gamblers by gambling type.
candidates.abstract: In gambling research, gambling subtypes have traditionally been used to distinguish between games of skill or competition and games of chance. The former are referred to as strategic games, whereas the latter are classified as non-strategic games. Despite their similarities, individuals who engage in strategic and non-strategic gambling exhibit distinct characteristics. Consequently, a substantial body of research has examined how gamblers differ according to the types of gambling activities in which they engage. These differences in gamblers' profiles have important implications for the clinical assessment and treatment of individuals with gambling problems. Nevertheless, heterogeneous classification methods have been used to define gambling subtypes, compromising the comparability and reproducibility of research findings and hindering the implementation of evidence-based recommendations for the regulation, prevention, and treatment of gambling disorder.

candidates.title: VIP-Mediated Syndromes: Contrasting Presentations and Multidisciplinary Management of Two Rare Neuroendocrine Tumors.
candidates.abstract: Vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-secreting tumors are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms that cause severe secretory diarrhea and electrolyte abnormalities. We describe 2 atypical cases requiring multidisciplinary care. One patient had a VIP-secreting pheochromocytoma with elevated VIP and metanephrine levels; symptoms improved after adrenalectomy. The second had a metastatic small intestinal neuroendocrine tumor with persistent VIP-mediated diarrhea despite debulking and somatostatin analog therapy, complicated by anal fissures, trans-sphincteric perianal fistula, and neuropathic pelvic pain. These cases highlight morbidity and potential complications associated with extrapancreatic VIP hypersecretion and the value of coordinated multidisciplinary management to improve outcomes and quality of life.

candidates.title: [Conservative treatment of non-unions : Options and limitations].
candidates.abstract: Despite modern medical care, non-unions occur in 2-5% of all fractures. The burden on patients involves prolonged rehabilitation and potentially further surgery. Costs for healthcare systems increase substantially. While surgical intervention represents the standard of care, a range of non-surgical treatment options is available. A particular advantage of non-surgical treatment is the avoidance of surgery itself. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound therapy (LIPUS) and the use of pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMF) are painless and applied by patients themselves once daily. With focused extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT), administration by a physician-usually under general anesthesia-ensures the treatment takes effect precisely at the target site. Bony defects up to 5-10 mm in size can be treated without surgery, provided there is no infection and mechanical stability is adequate. Pseudarthrosen treten trotz moderner medizinischer Versorgung bei 2–5 % der Frakturen auf. Die Belastung für betroffene PatientInnen ist hoch, die Kosten für das Gesundheitssystem vervielfältigen sich. Während die operative Therapie den Standard in der Versorgung darstellt, bestehen auch nichtoperative Therapiemöglichkeiten. Vorteil der nichtoperativen Behandlung ist die Vermeidung einer erneuten Operation, insbesondere bei erhöhtem perioperativen Risiko. Die niedrigdosierte gepulste Ultraschalltherapie (NGU) und die Anwendung pulsierender elektromagnetischer Felder (PEMF) sind schmerzfrei und werden von den PatientInnen selbstständig durchgeführt. Bei der fokussierten extrakorporalen Stoßwellentherapie (ESWT) ist durch die ärztliche Applikation, meist im Rahmen einer Allgemeinanästhesie, die Wirkung am Zielort sichergestellt. Bei knöchernen Defekten bis zu einer Größe von 5 bis 10 mm kann eine konservative Therapie in Erwägung gezogen werden, sofern kein Infekt vorliegt und mechanische Stabilität gegeben ist.

candidates.title: Sexual Health in Females with Multiple Sclerosis of Reproductive Age.
candidates.abstract: Sexual dysfunction is highly prevalent among females with multiple sclerosis (FwMS), yet it remains under-recognized and inadequately integrated into routine care. This review examines sexual health in FwMS of reproductive age, with particular attention to assessment, reproductive considerations, and management. Sexual dysfunction in FwMS is often multifactorial, with contributions from neurological, physical, psychological, and relationship-related factors. Sexual dysfunction and disease-related factors may indirectly influence sexual activity, conception, and reproductive decision-making. Preconception counselling should incorporate sexual health alongside disease activity and treatment considerations. Evidence regarding sexual function during pregnancy and postpartum in FwMS remains limited. Management is individualized and may include symptom optimization, pelvic floor therapy, exercise, psychological and couples-based interventions, and selected pharmacologic therapies. Sexual health should be incorporated into comprehensive MS care, particularly during reproductive transitions. Prospective studies across preconception, pregnancy, and postpartum periods and randomized trials of interventions in FwMS are needed to guide evidence-based care.

candidates.title: Multiple Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Postoperative Residual Tumor in Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors.
candidates.abstract: To develop and validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model for predicting radiologically confirmed postoperative residual tumor (RT) in pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). We retrospectively analyzed 584 surgically treated patients with PitNETs from a single center, using a random 7:3 training-test split and internal cross-validation. The primary endpoint was radiologically confirmed postoperative RT, assessed using MRI obtained within 48 h after surgery and longitudinal follow-up MRI. Candidate variables were selected using LASSO regression, with nine ML algorithms developed. Discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, interobserver agreement, and SHAP-based interpretability were assessed. Postoperative RT occurred in 72 patients (12.3%). Sensitivity analysis showed high agreement between 48-h MRI and follow-up confirmation (96.4%; Cohen's kappa = 0.837). Interobserver agreement was high for retrosellar invasion (kappa = 0.825), internal carotid artery invasion (kappa = 0.960), and Knosp grade (quadratic weighted kappa = 0.994). Eight predictors were retained: maximum sagittal diameter, maximum coronal diameter, age, Knosp grade, internal carotid artery invasion, sphenoid sinus pneumatization, tumor consistency, and retrosellar invasion. In the internal test set, the random forest model achieved high discrimination (AUC = 0.945; accuracy = 0.938), with performance comparable to LightGBM and XGBoost in DeLong testing. LightGBM had the lowest Brier score. Random forest was selected for the web tool after internal evaluation, with discrimination comparable to LightGBM, XGBoost, and SVM. Its generalizability to other centers and future patient cohorts remains unproven because evaluation used only a single-center random split and internal cross-validation. External and temporal validation with calibration assessment is needed before clinical implementation.

candidates.title: Percutaneous and endovascular procedures in adrenal disease: indications, technique, and outcomes.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

candidates.title: Characterizing bone metastases and skeletal-related events in patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms utilizing 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography.
candidates.abstract: Tumors of neuroendocrine origin are a heterogenous group of related neoplasms which can arise from anywhere in the body. Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are categorized by site of origin, differentiation status and grade (Ki-67 expression and/or mitotic rate), with significant prognostic variability accordingly. Historically, the prevalence of bone metastasis is reported to be 6%-12% based on "first generation" (i.e., 111Indium pentetreotide [Octreoscan®]) somatostatin receptor imaging (SSRI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study including patients with well-differentiated NENs to determine the clinical and imaging characteristics of osseous metastases when evaluated with higher-sensitivity 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scans, as well as determining fracture prevalence in selected sub-cohorts. We also developed a risk score analysis to assess risk of fracture in this cohort. Four hundred twenty-four patients were identified for inclusion. The median age was 61 years. Most patients were asymptomatic (64%), had sclerotic lesions (77%), Krenning 4 (71%), and had >3 sites (69%) of osseous disease. A high proportion of patients had osseous metastases at sites with high risk for fracture, including vertebra (82%), pelvis (63%), and peri-trochanteric femur (34%). Fifty-seven patients (13%) in the entire cohort suffered a fracture. Fracture prevalence was significantly lower in small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs, 7%) and Grades 1 and 2 disease (8% and 9%, respectively), with higher prevalence in pancreatic NETs, paragangliomas/pheochromocytomas, lung carcinoid, and Grade 3 disease (≥20% for each; p-values <.05). Our study showed that the rate of osseous metastatic disease approximates 20% in well-differentiated NENs. Most bone metastases are asymptomatic and the risk of fracture is variable based on the primary site of disease and tumor grade. Our novel risk score analysis for fracture was designed to assist clinician decision making as to management of bone metastasis in this patient population.

candidates.title: Addison's Disease Mimicking Cerebral Salt Wasting Syndrome: A Case of Severe Hyponatremia.
candidates.abstract: Hyponatremia is a common electrolyte abnormality with varying degrees of severity. It can be asymptomatic if mild and can cause convulsions and coma if severe. Systematic investigation of hyponatremia helps to find out the etiology and proper management. Here, we are presenting the case of a 67-year-old man who presented with vomiting, hyperpigmentation, and hypovolemic hyponatremia due to Addison's disease. Evaluation of hyponatremia showed elevated urinary sodium as expected in Addison's disease, but there was hypouricemia with increased fractional excretion of uric acid suggestive of cerebral salt wasting syndrome. Even with the correct diagnosis, wrong medication interval can cause inadequate rise in serum sodium. Mild thyroid-stimulating hormone elevation can occur in untreated isolated Addison's disease. Addison's disease should always be considered in unexplained hyponatremia even if laboratory findings are suggestive of cerebral salt wasting syndrome. Hyponatremia in Addison's disease may respond poorly to hypertonic saline until glucocorticoid deficiency is corrected, and steroid and fluid replacement is essential and lifesaving.

candidates.title: Utility of the ACTH/cortisol ratio for differentiating pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism.
candidates.abstract: No simple, blood-based biomarker to estimate tumor size in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism (PDH) has been evaluated. Determine whether the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)/cortisol ratio differentiates pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with PDH and correlates with pituitary size. Seventy privately-owned dogs with PDH (microadenomas, n = 30; macroadenomas, n = 40). Retrospective multicenter observational study. Endogenous ACTH and cortisol concentrations obtained at the same time point before treatment were used to calculate the ACTH/cortisol ratio. Pituitary tumor size was classified using the pituitary-to-brain (P/B) ratio. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and multivariable logistic regression. Dogs with macroadenomas had significantly higher ACTH/cortisol ratios than dogs with microadenomas (median, 9.12; IQR, 6.46-14.28 vs median, 4.90; IQR, 3.08-8.10; P < .001). The ratio showed moderate discrimination for differentiating macroadenomas from microadenomas with an area under the curve of 0.77 (95% CI, 0.66-0.89; P < .001). A cutoff >5.69 yielded 85% sensitivity and 60% specificity (positive likelihood ratio 2.13), whereas a higher ratio >11.74 achieved 90% specificity and 35% sensitivity (positive likelihood ratio 3.50). The ACTH/cortisol ratio showed moderate positive correlation with pituitary size (Spearman's ρ = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.26-0.64; P < .001) and remained independently associated with macroadenoma classification in multivariable analysis (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.05-1.40). The ACTH/cortisol ratio is associated with pituitary tumor size in dogs with PDH and may support clinical risk stratification, particularly when advanced imaging is unavailable.

candidates.title: Acute Sheehan Syndrome Presenting as Panhypopituitarism and Reversible Cardiac Dysfunction in a Patient With Sickle Cell Disease: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sheehan syndrome is an uncommon cause of hypopituitarism resulting from ischemic pituitary necrosis following severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) and hypotension. Its presentation can be delayed and non-specific, and it is rarely reported in the context of mild PPH with severe hemolysis. Here, we describe a 31-year-old woman with underlying sickle cell disease (SCD) who developed panhypopituitarism and reversible cardiac dysfunction after an 11-week period of progressive symptoms following spontaneous vaginal delivery complicated by an estimated blood loss of 700 mL and severe hemolysis. Pituitary hormonal replacement therapy, together with heart failure treatment, resulted in marked clinical and biochemical improvement, with normalization of metabolic abnormalities and recovery of cardiac function. This case suggests a possible association between Sheehan syndrome and postpartum blood loss of 700 mL accompanied by severe hemolysis, though this remains hypothetical based on a single case.

candidates.title: Pituitary Apoplexy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism in a Neurologically Complex Patient: A Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary apoplexy is a rare endocrine emergency resulting from either acute haemorrhage or infarction within the pituitary gland. Although apoplexy occurs most frequently in a pre-existing pituitary adenoma, apoplexy could be the first presentation of a previously unknown adenoma. Acute headaches, visual disturbances, and neurological symptoms are common presenting symptoms in apoplexy; however, these symptoms may overlap with other neurological emergencies, which necessitate a holistic approach of clinical, radiological, and hormonal evaluation for suspected cases of apoplexy to confirm the diagnosis. Here we present a diagnostically challenging case of a 66-year-old man who presented with a sudden severe headache. His background history included a presumed intraventricular neurocytoma under surveillance. Initial CT head scan suggested possible haemorrhage within a known intraventricular mass (neurocytoma) with no obvious changes within the pituitary gland. However, subsequent MRI head demonstrated radiological features consistent with pituitary apoplexy. Later in his admission, he exhibited bilateral peripheral visual field constriction and early papilledema on fundoscopy. Hormonal testing showed evidence of hypopituitarism. The patient was managed conservatively with intravenous hydrocortisone replacement. During admission, he developed bilateral pulmonary emboli, for which he was treated with anticoagulation. While he was on anticoagulation, he developed intracranial haemorrhage, which led to his death after discharge from the hospital. This case demonstrates the importance of considering pituitary apoplexy in a challenging radiological and clinical presentation. A pre-existing neurological lesion (neurocytoma) makes a holistic approach, including MRI imaging and early hormonal evaluation are essential for timely diagnosis and treatment of pituitary apoplexy. The clinical challenge of having concurrent haemorrhagic and thrombotic events necessitates an individualised approach after balancing the benefits and risks of using anticoagulation treatment.

candidates.title: Association Between Pituitary Adenoma Excision and Risk of Cerebrovascular Disease and Mortality in Patients With Cushing's Disease: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
candidates.abstract: Cushing's disease (CD) is a hypercortisolemic state resulting from an adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma (PA). Cerebrovascular disease (CeVD) is a dangerous sequela of CD, yet few studies have characterized its risk in CD. This study aimed to report the risk of CeVD in CD patients with and without surgical treatment. This retrospective multicenter study from the TriNetX database included 20 years of data from 69 healthcare organizations. TriNetX was searched to identify adults in the United States with CD. We used 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) for demographic characteristics and tobacco use to identify a matched non-CD group. Risk ratios were calculated to identify the risk of CeVD. Among patients with CD, we identified those who underwent PA excision after diagnosis and determined associations with CeVD. We used 1:1 PSM matching for demographic characteristics and comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia) to identify a matched non-PA excision CD group. The CD group (n = 4265) was 78.4% female with a mean age at CD diagnosis of 45.7 years. After PSM, patients with CD had a significantly higher risk of any CeVD (risk ratio [RR] = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.70-2.29), ischemic stroke (RR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.83-3.01), and hemorrhagic stroke (RR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.22-2.49). Stratification by sex identified similar associations. One thousand three hundred seventy-seven patients with CD who underwent PA excision were identified after matching. PA excision was associated with lower risk of any CeVD (RR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.55-0.86, number needed to treat [NNT] = 25.6), ischemic stroke (RR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.35-0.72, NNT = 33.3), and mortality (RR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.35-0.77, NNT = 40.0) compared with those who did not have excision. Sensitivity analyses using medication-based proxies for biochemical remission showed similar trends between curative and noncurative resection but were not statistically significant. This study demonstrated that patients with CD are at an increased risk of CeVD, including ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. PA excision for patients with CD may reduce lifetime CeVD risk and mortality.

candidates.title: Pregnancy in Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndrome Type 3c With Graves' Disease and Myasthenia Gravis: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 3c (APS3c), characterized by autoimmune thyroid disease with another organ-specific autoimmune disorder in the absence of adrenal insufficiency, is an uncommon presentation. Its coexistence with Graves' disease and myasthenia gravis (MG) is rare and poses additional diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when complicated by thyroid storm and pregnancy. We report the ongoing management of a 22-year-old woman with this combination of autoimmune disorders. She was admitted with thyroid storm diagnosed using the Burch-Wartofsky Point Scale and Japan Thyroid Association criteria after a 15-month history of weight loss, heat intolerance, diaphoresis, anxiety, palpitations, unilateral ptosis, and fatigable proximal upper-extremity weakness. Graves' disease and MG were diagnosed based on clinical findings, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin and acetylcholine receptor antibodies, and electrophysiological evidence of a postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder. In the absence of clinical or biochemical evidence of primary adrenal insufficiency, the coexistence of autoimmune thyroid disease and MG supported a diagnosis of APS3c on the Neufeld and Blizzard classification. Despite methimazole (15 mg/day) and pyridostigmine (600 mg/day) therapy, and good adherence to treatment, biochemical hyperthyroidism persisted and progressed to thyroid storm. During outpatient follow-up, an intrauterine pregnancy was confirmed. Methimazole was withheld during the first trimester while the patient remained clinically stable despite persistent biochemical hyperthyroidism, and it was resumed thereafter. At the time of writing, the pregnancy remains ongoing under multidisciplinary care involving endocrinology, neurology, internal medicine, and maternal-fetal medicine, with serial maternal monitoring, planned third-trimester antibody reassessment, targeted fetal ultrasonography, perinatal planning, and neonatal surveillance. This case highlights APS3c as an important diagnostic framework for the coexistence of Graves' disease and MG and illustrates how management must be continually reassessed in the setting of thyroid storm and pregnancy. Maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes remain pending.

candidates.title: Scleroderma-Like Phenotype in a Patient With Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis and Acromegaly: A Triple Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, and acromegaly are rare disorders that share several clinical manifestations, including skin thickening, heart failure, dysphagia, fatigue, and soft tissue enlargement. Their coexistence is exceptionally rare and poses a significant diagnostic challenge, increasing the risk of premature diagnostic closure. We report a 78-year-old man who developed progressive diffuse skin thickening following spinal cord stimulator revision. Positive RNA polymerase III antibodies supported a diagnosis of diffuse systemic sclerosis. Evaluation of worsening edema and exertional dyspnea revealed severe concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with relative apical sparing on echocardiography, and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy confirmed transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Persistent macroglossia, coarse facial features, prior carpal tunnel syndrome, and a remote history of increasing ring and shoe size prompted endocrine evaluation, which demonstrated elevated insulin-like growth factor-1 levels, failure of growth hormone suppression, and a pituitary macroadenoma consistent with acromegaly. The patient underwent successful transsphenoidal resection with biochemical remission. This case highlights the importance of reconsidering the differential diagnosis when clinical features are not fully explained by an established diagnosis. Recognizing atypical and discordant findings prevented premature diagnostic closure and led to the identification of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and acromegaly in a patient with a rapidly progressive scleroderma-like phenotype.

candidates.title: No significant differences in complication and graft failure rates by type of surgery or osteotomy level after slope-reducing osteotomy with ACL reconstruction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract: To determine whether anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) graft failure and complication rates differ by type of surgery, osteotomy level, or planned surgical stages in patients undergoing anterior closing wedge high tibial osteotomy combined with ACL reconstruction. A systematic review and meta-analysis searched MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Epistemonikos up to September 2026 for studies reporting complications in adults undergoing anterior closing wedge high tibial osteotomy with anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction. Paired reviewers independently screened, extracted, and assessed quality. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated overall proportions and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analyses evaluated differences by type of surgery (primary vs. revision ACL reconstruction), osteotomy level (supratubercular, transtubercular or infratubercular), and number of planned surgical stages (single- or two-stage procedures). Sixteen observational studies comprising 664 patients (673 knees) were included. The estimated graft failure proportion was 1.7% (95% CI: 0.3%-7.9%), with no significant differences by type of surgery (p = 0.091), osteotomy level (p = 0.770) or planned stages (p = 0.736). Frequent postoperative events included symptomatic hardware (7.8%) and complication-related reintervention (4.4%). Major complications were uncommon, including delayed union or non-union (0.4%), deep infections (0.2%), and vascular or thromboembolic events (0.1%). Complication-related reinterventions differed significantly by osteotomy level (p = 0.0016), being higher with multiple techniques compared to infratubercular and supratubercular approaches. Postoperative recurvatum differed significantly by type of surgery (p = 0.0037). The certainty of evidence was rated very low for all outcomes. Anterior closing wedge high tibial osteotomy combined with ACL reconstruction showed a consistent, low-complication safety profile across type of surgery, osteotomy levels, and planned stages, though very low certainty of evidence indicates insufficient power to detect differences rather than demonstrated equivalence. These findings do not inform optimal treatment strategy or timing, and further prospective comparative studies are needed to define the incremental benefit of slope correction relative to isolated reconstruction. Level IV, systematic review and meta-analysis.
candidates.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA

candidates.title: Retinal Microvascular and Peripapillary Profiles in Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Versus Nonfunctioning Adrenal Adenomas.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is associated with increased cardiometabolic morbidity, but its relationship with the retinal microcirculation is unknown. We compared retinal and peripapillary microvascular parameters between MACS and nonfunctioning adrenal adenoma (NFA) and, secondarily, examined their associations with continuously modeled post-dexamethasone cortisol. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study, 98 patients (45 NFA, 53 MACS) were included, and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and structural OCT data from one eye per patient were analyzed. The primary outcome was whole-image deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; secondary analyses were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (q values). Results: OCTA was evaluable in 89 patients. The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups in the main analysis (NFA vs. MACS, 48.64 ± 5.71% vs. 47.31 ± 5.77%; adjusted difference -1.29 percentage points, 95% CI -3.97 to 1.38; p = 0.339) or in any sensitivity analysis. In secondary analyses, superior retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness was greater in MACS (β = 17.38 µm; q < 0.001) and increased with ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) (β = 13.74 µm; q = 0.010). Higher ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) was also associated with lower parafoveal DCP (β = -2.72 percentage points; p = 0.013) and inside-disc radial peripapillary capillary vessel density (β = -3.13 percentage points; p = 0.026), which did not survive multiplicity correction; no superficial capillary plexus sector was associated with either exposure (all p ≥ 0.37). Conclusions: MACS was not significantly associated with whole-image DCP vessel density. The secondary associations with continuous cortisol are cross-sectional and hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

candidates.title: Joint-preserving correction of malunited anterior and posterior malleolar fractures.
candidates.abstract: The posterior and anterior rims of the distal tibial are essential for overall ankle function. They are referred to as third and fourth malleolus, respectively, which are commonly injured in the wake of ankle fractures. Residual displacement, malunion, or nonunion may cause fibular malposition in the tibial incisura (fibular notch), syndesmotic (tibiofibular mortise) instability, and joint incongruency leading to posttraumatic arthritis. Computed tomography scanning is required to assess the three-dimensional outline of the deformity and to make an appropriate treatment plan. Correction of anterior and posterior malleolar malalignment aims at restoring the following: (1) articular tibiotalar congruency, (2) sagittal ankle bone stability and talar containment, (3) the anatomy of the tibial incisura (fibular notch) to enable correct positioning of the distal fibula, and (4) tibiofibular alignment and syndesmotic (mortise) stability. To date, there is little evidence in the literature regarding the outcome of realignment of anterior and posterior malleolar malunions, and further studies are needed to establish evidence-based guidelines for surgical correction. Die Hinter- und Vorderkante des distalen Schienbeins sind für die Gesamtfunktion des oberen Sprunggelenks von entscheidender Bedeutung. Sie werden als dritter bzw. vierter Malleolus bezeichnet und sind bei Sprunggelenksfrakturen häufig mitverletzt. Verbliebene Fehlstellungen, Fehlheilungen oder Pseudarthrosen können zu einer Fehlstellung der Fibula in der Tibiainzisur, zu einer Instabilität des Syndesmosenkomplexes und zu einer Gelenkinkongruenz führen, was wiederum eine posttraumatische Arthrose zur Folge haben kann. Zur Beurteilung des dreidimensionalen Verlaufs der Deformität und zur Erstellung eines geeigneten Behandlungsplans ist eine Computertomographie erforderlich. Die Korrektur einer Fehlstellung der Tibiavorder- und -hinterkante zielt auf die Wiederherstellung von: (1) der Gelenkkongruenz zwischen Tibia und Talus, (2) der sagittalen Stabilität des Talus, (3) der Anatomie und Integrität der Tibiainzisur, um eine korrekte Positionierung der distalen Fibula zu ermöglichen, und (4) des tibiofibularen Alignments und der Stabilität der Syndesmosenkomplexes (Knöchelgabel). In der Literatur gibt es bislang nur wenige Angaben zu den Ergebnissen der gelenkerhaltenden Korrektur von Fehlstellungen des anterioren und posterioren Malleolus, und es sind weitere Studien erforderlich, um evidenzbasierte Leitlinien für die chirurgische Korrektur zu erstellen.

candidates.title: Beyond Digoxin Toxicity: A Fatal Case of BRASH Syndrome Triggered by Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
candidates.abstract: Bradycardia, renal failure, atrioventricular (AV) nodal blockade, shock, and hyperkalemia (BRASH) syndrome is a rare, life-threatening clinical condition caused by the synergistic interaction between hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction, and AV nodal blocking agents, resulting in severe bradycardia and hemodynamic instability. Early recognition is often challenging due to its nonspecific presentation. We report the case of an 82-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, ischemic heart disease, congestive cardiac failure, chronic kidney disease, and chronic digoxin therapy who presented with abdominal pain, confusion, dizziness, hypotension, and profound bradycardia. Investigations demonstrated severe hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury on top of chronic kidney disease, hyponatremia, and electrocardiographic changes consistent with hyperkalemia. Initial differential diagnoses included mesenteric ischemia, adrenal insufficiency, and digoxin toxicity; however, imaging excluded bowel ischemia, cortisol levels were normal, and serum digoxin at the therapeutic level. Community-acquired pneumonia complicated by sepsis was identified as the precipitating trigger for BRASH syndrome. Despite intensive treatment, including hyperkalemia management, isoprenaline infusion, antibiotics, corticosteroids, and supportive care, the patient's condition progressively deteriorated, culminating in multiorgan failure and death shortly afterward. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of BRASH syndrome and emphasizes the importance of early recognition and targeted management to interrupt the vicious cycle and improve clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: [Reference guide for the clinical management of adult Langerhans cell histiocytosis (key points from the first edition, 2025)].
candidates.abstract: According to the registry of the Japanese Society of Hematology, adult histiocytic neoplasms are extremely rare, with approximately 40 cases reported annually, and the most common among them is Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH). Lesions may involve multiple organs, including bone, skin, lung, the central nervous system, and the endocrine system. Without a hematology perspective, the neoplastic nature of LCH may not be apparent, resulting in missed diagnoses. Central diabetes insipidus, anterior pituitary dysfunction, and LCH-associated neurodegeneration, once developed, often result in irreversible impairment. Because delayed therapeutic intervention can result in permanent organ damage, it is essential for hematologists to understand the "minimum initial management" required to protect patient outcomes. This review summarizes the key points of diagnosis and initial management in adult LCH based on the first edition of the Adult LCH Clinical Reference Guide (2025).
candidates.journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology

candidates.title: Hotspot mutations and tumour spectrum in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome: genotype-phenotype analysis of a large Chinese cohort.
candidates.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant multisystem tumour syndrome caused by germline VHL mutations. The traditional classification of VHL syndrome, which is largely based on pheochromocytoma penetrance, is insufficient for individualised surveillance and management. This study aimed to improve mutation-specific risk stratification and define genotype-phenotype correlations of recurrent hotspot mutations in a large Chinese cohort. This retrospective single-centre study included 674 patients with VHL disease from 283 unrelated families. Four recurrent hotspot mutation subtypes were analysed: codon 65 missense mutations, exon 2 deletion, c.481C > T, and c.224_226del. Kaplan-Meier analysis and univariate and multivariate Cox regression models were used to assess age-related tumour risks and survival outcomes. Codon 65 missense mutations were associated with a lower risk of retinal angioma and pheochromocytoma, indicating a relatively mild phenotype. Exon 2 deletion was characterised by a higher prevalence, earlier onset, and increased age-related risk of retinal angioma and worse renal cell carcinoma (RCC)-specific survival. Increased prevalences and age-related risks of central nervous system hemangioblastoma (CHB), RCC, and pancreatic cysts or tumours were associated with c.481C > T mutations. The c.224_226del subtype showed a distinct CHB-predominant phenotype, with higher CHB incidence, earlier onset, lower pancreatic lesion risk, and higher overall mortality. Recurrent hotspot VHL mutation subtypes were associated with distinct clinical phenotypes and prognostic patterns. Mutation subtype-based classification (covering 19.6% of patients with VHL syndrome) may provide more precise guidance for surveillance, clinical decision-making, and genetic counselling than traditional broad classification models.
candidates.journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology

candidates.title: Management of congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency: an update.
candidates.abstract: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) represents a group of autosomal recessive disorders characterized by enzyme deficiencies thatimpair adrenal steroidogenesis, most commonly due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. The biochemical defects in CAH translate to a spectrumof clinical consequences, which include adrenal insufficiency, genital ambiguity or disordered sex development, infertility, short stature,and an increased risk of metabolic syndrome during adolescence and adulthood. The severity and clinical features of CAH vary dependingon the enzymatic defect, residual enzymatic activity, the age of presentation, and genotype. This review comprehensively covers the genetic background, classification, and clinical spectrum of CAH, including classical and non-classical forms. We discuss the importance and implementation of neonatal screening programs for early diagnosis and intervention. Specialattention is given to differences in treatment approaches between children and adolescents, highlighting the challenges of optimizingglucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid therapy across developmental stages. Furthermore, we present emerging novel pharmacologicalagents currently in clinical trials aimed at improving disease management. The review also addresses potential complications associatedwith CAH, such as metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular risks, and bone health issues. Emphasizing a patient-centered approach, wehighlight the critical role of experienced endocrinologists in delivering individualized care to improve long-term outcomes. Our review summarizes the current knowledge, aims to guide clinicians in evidence-based management and highlights ongoing research into innovativetherapies for CAH.

candidates.title: Synovial plica syndromes: a comprehensive overview from embryology to pathology.
candidates.abstract: Synovial plicae are folds of synovial tissue in the knee, hip, elbow, and shoulder, representing embryonic remnants of synovial septa. They are usually asymptomatic, but trauma, repetitive microtrauma, or prior surgery can render them thickened and fibrotic, producing pain and mechanical symptoms collectively termed plica syndrome. It is easily overlooked or misdiagnosed because the symptoms are nonspecific and other intra-articular disorders often coexist. This review addresses the embryology, histology, anatomy, clinical presentation, imaging, and treatment of synovial plicae across these joints, with emphasis on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. MRI is the preferred imaging modality for evaluating suspected plica syndrome, characterizing the fold and associated abnormalities, and excluding alternative causes of joint pain. Pathologic plicae appear thickened and irregular, with increased signal intensity and frequently associated focal synovitis or adjacent chondral damage. Plica thickness alone has limited diagnostic value, as measurements overlap between symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. Establishing a diagnosis of symptomatic plica syndrome requires correlation of the imaging findings with the clinical presentation. When joint effusion is absent, magnetic resonance (MR) or computed tomography (CT) arthrography improves delineation of the synovial folds and associated lesions. Plica syndrome occurs most often in young, physically active patients, and management is initially conservative. When symptoms are refractory, arthroscopic resection relieves symptoms, particularly when the plica is the only abnormality and the cartilage is preserved. Most outcome data derive from the knee and the elbow.

candidates.title: Calcified foraminal metastasis from ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma mimicking a nerve sheath tumor.
candidates.abstract: Ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma (OLGSC) is an uncommon subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, characterized by an indolent clinical course with potential for late local recurrence and metastatic disease. Musculoskeletal involvement is rare. We report a case of late OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly growing, thoracic foraminal mass in a 55-year-old woman, 33 years after initial cancer treatment. Rising CA-125 levels prompted 18F-FDG PET/CT, which revealed an FDG-avid mass in the left T9-T10 neural foramen (SUVmax 6.6). CT demonstrated foraminal widening and intralesional calcifications, while MRI showed a dumbbell-shaped mass extending into the epidural space and left costovertebral region, with heterogeneous signal intensity and mild diffuse heterogeneous enhancement. Retrospective review of a CT examination performed 12 years earlier revealed a smaller foraminal mass without visible calcifications. Given its location and morphology, the lesion initially suggested a nerve sheath tumor, while the presence of calcifications also raised the possibility of a chondroid lesion. Although nonspecific, calcifications are recognized in primary and metastatic OLGSC. The combination of increased FDG uptake and the patient's oncologic history, raised suspicion of metastatic disease. Image-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic OLGSC with psammoma bodies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly progressive, calcified paravertebral and foraminal mas mimicking a nerve sheath tumor. This case emphasizes the need for careful evaluation of atypical masses in patients with a history of cancer, even decades after initial treatment, and the importance of biopsy for diagnostic confirmation.
